topic.subject: social
topic.title: Weavers, iron smelters and factory owners
topic.scope: Indian textiles, decline of weaving, Manchester imports, iron smelting, Tata steel

misconceptions.statement: Indian weavers were poor and unskilled laborers who only made basic clothes.
misconceptions.why: Students often equate historical poverty with a lack of skill, ignoring the global prestige of Indian textiles.
misconceptions.fix: Indian weavers were highly skilled artisans whose fine muslins and chintz were world-famous and in high demand globally.

probe.question: Why were Indian textiles in such high demand in Europe before the 18th century?
probe.wrong_answer: Because they were cheap and made by unskilled laborers who worked for very low wages.

concepts.name: Impact of Industrial Revolution and Manchester Imports

misconceptions.statement: Indian weavers lost their jobs only because they refused to use new machines.
misconceptions.why: Students often blame the victim's lack of adaptation rather than systemic colonial economic policies.
misconceptions.fix: Weavers lost their livelihoods because British colonial policies imposed heavy duties on Indian goods while flooding India with cheap, machine-made British textiles.

probe.question: What was the main reason for the decline of the Indian weaving industry?
probe.wrong_answer: The weavers were too stubborn to learn how to operate the new machines from England.

misconceptions.statement: Indian iron smelting died out because the iron produced was of very poor quality.
misconceptions.why: Students assume that if a traditional craft disappeared, it must have been inferior to modern methods.
misconceptions.fix: Indian wootz steel was of exceptional quality; the industry declined due to strict colonial forest laws that restricted access to wood and charcoal.

probe.question: Why did the traditional iron smelting furnaces in India stop working?
probe.wrong_answer: The iron they produced was weak and could not be used for building modern structures.

misconceptions.statement: The British government actively encouraged and funded the setup of Tata Steel in India.
misconceptions.why: Students often assume that colonial infrastructure projects were always supported by the British rulers.
misconceptions.fix: The British were reluctant to support Indian-owned industries and preferred importing steel from Britain; TISCO was established despite colonial resistance.

probe.question: How did the British government react to the establishment of the Tata Iron and Steel Company?
probe.wrong_answer: They were very happy and provided all the money and support needed to build the factory.
